<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation of
Directors&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Directors who are not executive officers of our
company are paid $20,000 per year, paid quarterly as a retainer, as well as $1,500
per meeting for each of the quarterly board meetings they attend. These
directors are also paid $500 per telephonic meeting, $750 per audit committee
meeting and $500 for all other committee meetings. In addition, the chairman of
the audit committee is paid $2,000 annually as a retainer; other committee
chairs are paid $1,000 annually as a retainer. Directors who are not executive
officers are granted options to purchase 1,500 shares of our common stock each
year. Newly appointed directors receive a one-time grant of options to purchase
10,000 shares of our common stock. We also reimburse all of our directors for
reasonable travel expenses incurred in attending our meetings. Employee
directors are not compensated for their services as directors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;28, 2005, in
conjunction with our IPO, we granted Messrs.&nbsp;Bloom and Eugster each an
option under the 2004 Plan to purchase 10,000 shares of common stock at an
exercise price of $14.00 per share. The options were 50% vested on the grant
date and the remaining 50% will vest on the first anniversary of the grant
date. On February&nbsp;8, 2006, we granted each non-employee director, except Mr.&nbsp;Healy,
who declined receipt of the option, an option under the 2004 Plan to purchase
1,500 shares of common stock at an exercise price of $18.77 per share. The
options vested immediately upon grant.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employment
contracts and termination of employment and change-in-control arrangements.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have employment agreements with all seven of our
executive officers. On December&nbsp;31, 1997, we entered into employment
agreements with Mr.&nbsp;Zanatta and Mr.&nbsp;Maanum pursuant to which Mr.&nbsp;Zanatta
is serving as our President and Chief Executive Officer and Mr.&nbsp;Maanum is
serving as our Chief Operating Officer. On January&nbsp;6, 2003, we entered
into an employment agreement with Michael&nbsp;W. McCormick pursuant to which
he is serving as our Chief Marketing Officer. On March&nbsp;15, 2004, we
entered into an </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">employment agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Nordvold
pursuant to which he is serving as our Chief Financial Officer. On May&nbsp;11,
2005, we entered into an employment agreement with Mr.&nbsp;Hornbaker pursuant
to which he is serving as our Senior Vice President&#151;Sales and Operations. On March&nbsp;16,
2006, concurrent with the completion of our acquisition of The GolfWorks, we
entered into employment agreements with each of Mr.&nbsp;Maltby, pursuant to
which he is serving as our Senior Vice President&#151;Chief Technology Officer,
Research and Development, and Mark R. McCormick, pursuant to which he is
serving as our Senior Vice President&#151;CEO of The GolfWorks.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each employment agreement will continue in effect
until either party terminates it. Pursuant to the terms of each employment
agreement, the executive officer receives, among other things, an annual base
salary as determined by the board of directors and a bonus from time to time at
the sole discretion of the board of directors. In the event we terminate the
executive officer&#146;s employment without cause or the executive officer
terminates his employment with us for good reason, we must pay to the executive
officer his then-current annual base salary for the six-month period
immediately following his termination of employment, plus any bonuses that the
executive officer would have received had he remained an employee during the
six-month period following his termination assuming all performance criteria
had been met. We must also continue for such six-month period to provide
benefits to the executive officer at the same levels and with the expenses
allocated as they were immediately before the executive officer&#146;s termination.
In addition, all options granted to the executive officer would immediately
vest and become exercisable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, pursuant to his employment agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Michael
W.&nbsp;McCormick received a grant of options to purchase 100,000 shares of our
common stock and reimbursement of relocation and moving expenses. Pursuant to
his employment agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Nordvold received a grant of options to
purchase 75,000 shares of common stock. Upon his employment in May&nbsp;2000, Mr.&nbsp;Hornbaker
received a grant of options to purchase 20,000 shares of common stock. Pursuant
to the terms of their respective employment agreements, Mr.&nbsp;Maltby and Mr.&nbsp;Mark
R. McCormick each received a grant of options to purchase 100,000 shares of
common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;31, 1997, we entered into retention
agreements with Mr.&nbsp;Zanatta and Mr.&nbsp;Maanum. In the event we terminate
the executive officer&#146;s employment in connection with a change in control or
within one year after a change in control, and other than for cause or
initiated by the executive officer for other than good reason, we must pay to
the executive officer his then-current annual base salary for the six-month
period immediately following his termination of employment, plus any bonuses
that the executive officer would have received had he remained an employee
during the six-month period following his termination assuming all performance
criteria had been met. We must also continue for such six-month period to
provide benefits to the executive officer at the same levels and with the
expenses allocated as they were immediately before the executive officer&#146;s
termination. In addition, all options granted to the executive officer would
immediately vest and become exercisable. Each retention agreement may be
terminated on August&nbsp;31 of any year by the affirmative vote of a majority
of the board of directors prior to June&nbsp;1 of that year and prior to the
occurrence or active consideration of a change in control.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each executive officer has
agreed, for the period of his employment with us and for a period of six months
thereafter, that he will not compete with us and he will not solicit our
employees to terminate their employment with us. In addition, in connection
with our acquisition of The GolfWorks in March&nbsp;2006, we entered into
restrictive covenant agreements with each of Mr.&nbsp;Maltby and Mr.&nbsp;Mark
R. McCormick. Pursuant to the restrictive covenant agreements, each of Mr.&nbsp;Maltby
and Mr.&nbsp;Mark R. McCormick has agreed, for a period of five years, that he
will not compete with us and he will not solicit our employees to terminate
their employment with us. The noncompete obligations in Mr.&nbsp;Mark R.
McCormick&#146;s restrictive covenant agreement will expire in the event of a change
in control.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additional information with respect to Compensation

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Compensation
Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2006,
Messrs.&nbsp;Bloom, Gellman and Newmark served as the members of our
compensation committee. No executive officer currently serves, or in the past
has served, on the compensation committee or the board of directors of any
other company of which any of the members of our compensation committee or any
of our directors is an executive officer.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 12.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Security
Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related <a name="Item12_SecurityOwnershipOfCertain_122117"></a>Stockholder Matters.</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities
authorized for issuance under equity compensation plans.</font></i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock Incentive
Plans</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1996 Stock Option
and Incentive Plan.</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i></b>Pursuant to our 1996 Stock Option
and Incentive Plan, as amended (1996 Plan), we have reserved 1,000,000 shares
of our common stock for issuance to persons who provide services to us or to
our affiliates as an employee, consultant or other service provider. The types
of awards that may be granted under the 1996 Plan include incentive and
non-qualified stock options and restricted stock. Under the 1996 Plan, our
compensation committee determines when and to whom awards will be granted, the
form of each award, the amount of each award, and any other terms or conditions
of each award consistent with the terms of the 1996 Plan. Each award agreement
specifies the number and type of award, together with any other terms and
conditions as determined by the compensation committee.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All stock options granted under the 1996 Plan will
expire no later than 121&nbsp;months from the date the options were granted,
and the exercise price for incentive stock options may not be less than 100% of
the fair market value of the shares at the time the option is granted. Options
granted under the 1996 Plan may be designated as exercisable in one or more
installments, upon the happening of certain events, upon the fulfillment of
certain conditions or upon such other terms and conditions as may be determined
upon grant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted stock awards granted under the 1996 Plan
entitle the holder to receive shares of our common stock, subject to forfeiture
if specified conditions are not satisfied at the end of a specified period.
During the period when the shares of our common stock are restricted, the
holder will not be permitted to transfer the shares, but will have all of the
rights of a shareholder in our company with respect to such shares, including
the right to vote the shares and receive dividends and other distributions with
respect to the shares.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2004 Stock
Incentive Plan.</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i></b>In July&nbsp;2004, our
shareholders approved our 2004 Stock Incentive Plan (2004 Plan), for which we
have reserved 1,000,000 shares of our common stock for issuance to directors,
officers, employees, consultants and other service providers of our company and
our affiliates. Like the 1996 Plan, the types of awards that may be granted
under the 2004 Plan include incentive and non-qualified stock options and
restricted stock. Under the 2004 Plan, our compensation committee determines
when and to whom awards will be granted, the form of each award, the amount of
each award, and any other terms or conditions of each award consistent with the
terms of the 2004 Plan.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All stock options granted under the 2004 Plan will
expire no later than ten years from the date the options were granted, and the
exercise price for incentive stock options may not be less than 100% of the
fair market value of the shares at the time the option is granted. Options
granted under the 2004 Plan may be designated as exercisable in one or more
installments, upon the happening of certain events, upon the </font></p>

such shares. The mailing address for each person listed is 7275 Flying Cloud

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 13.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Certain
Relationships and Related Transactions.<a name="Item13_CertainRelationshipsAndRel_123604"></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Acquisition of The GolfWorks.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">In March 2006, we acquired all of
the outstanding shares of The GolfWorks. Mark&nbsp;R. McCormick, our Senior Vice
President&#151;CEO of The GolfWorks, was an executive officer of The GolfWorks prior
to the acquisition and is the brother of Michael&nbsp;W. McCormick, our Chief
Marketing Officer. The purchase price, excluding direct costs of the
acquisition, consisted of $3.7&nbsp;million in cash ($500,000 of which has been
deposited into an indemnification escrow); 250,862&nbsp;shares of our common
stock valued at $4.8&nbsp;million based on the average closing price of our
common stock on the Nasdaq National Market during the five-day trading period
beginning three trading days prior to our announcement of the acquisition; and
warrants to purchase 150,000 shares of our common stock with a fair value of
$1.4&nbsp;million, determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The
warrants have an exercise price of $17.94 per share and a 10-year term expiring
on March&nbsp;16, 2016. In addition, we assumed $5.4&nbsp;million in debt from
The GolfWorks. Of the purchase price, Mark&nbsp;R. McCormick received an
allocation of $168,150 of the cash deposited in the indemnification escrow,
145,214 shares of our common stock, and a warrant to purchase 50,450 shares of
our common stock.</font></i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchase of
Inventory from The GolfWorks.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to our acquisition
of The GolfWorks in the first quarter of fiscal 2007, we purchased certain
inventory from The GolfWorks. Our decision to conduct business with The GolfWorks
was based on both qualitative and quantitative factors including product
offerings, pricing and customer service. Our Chief Executive Officer and Chief
Operating Officer reviewed our transactions with The GolfWorks, determined that
the transactions were at arm&#146;s-length and approved The GolfWorks as an
ongoing supplier of certain inventory. Total purchases from The GolfWorks
during fiscal 2004, 2005 and 2006 were $593,557, $727,573 and $1,352,374,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sublease of
Property from Best Buy Co.,&nbsp;Inc.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;6, 2004, we
entered into a sublease for our Gurnee, Illinois store with Best Buy Co.,&nbsp;Inc.
as sublessor. As of February&nbsp;25, 2006, Best Buy owned 1,276,001 shares of
our common stock. Thomas C. Healy, Best Buy&#146;s executive vice president-Best Buy
For Business, serves as a member of our board of directors. The terms of the
sublease provide that from December&nbsp;1, 2004 to January&nbsp;31, 2010,
minimum annual rent will be $232,499, or $19,375 per month. From February&nbsp;1,
2010 to January&nbsp;31, 2015, minimum annual rent will be $243,727, or $20,311
per month. The sublease will expire on January&nbsp;31, 2015. We began making
rent payments on December&nbsp;1, 2004. The total amount paid to Best Buy,
including payments for real estate taxes and common area charges, was $88,663
and $242,286 for fiscal 2005 and fiscal 2006, respectively.</font></p>

of our annual financial statements for the fiscal years ended February&nbsp;26,
2005, and February&nbsp;25, 2006; the audit of the consolidated financial
statements of Ralph Maltby Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc. for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005; the reviews of the financial statements included in our Quarterly Reports
on Form&nbsp;10-Q for the quarterly periods ended August&nbsp;27, 2005, and November&nbsp;26,
2005, respectively; and consultation on accounting matters. The audit fees for
fiscal 2006 include $178,800 for professional services rendered in connection
with our registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-1 (File No.&nbsp;333-125007)
that was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on July&nbsp;28,
2005 (i.e., our initial public offering).</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.5pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Consists

sharing plan. The audit-related fees for fiscal 2006 include $112,100 for due
diligence related to our acquisition of The GolfWorks.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.5pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Consists
of fees for tax advisory services in connection with the preparation of our tax
returns; claims for refund; tax planning; and tax audits and appeals.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consistent with SEC rules&nbsp;regarding auditor
independence, our audit committee has responsibility for appointing, setting
compensation and overseeing the work of the independent registered public
accounting firm. In recognition of this responsibility, and in accordance with
SEC rules&nbsp;and the Listing Standards of the Nasdaq National Market, it is
the policy of the committee to pre-approve all audit, audit-related, tax and
other permissible services proposed to be provided by the independent
registered public accounting firm. The fees listed above were pre-approved by
our audit committee pursuant to the committee&#146;s pre-approval policy.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Report of

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders<br>
Golf Galaxy,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the financial statements of Golf
Galaxy,&nbsp;Inc. as of February&nbsp;25, 2006, and February&nbsp;26, 2005, and
for each of the three years in the period ended February&nbsp;25, 2006, and
have issued our report thereon dated March&nbsp;31, 2006. Our audits also
included the financial statement schedule listed in Item 15(a)&nbsp;of
Form&nbsp;10-K. This schedule is the responsibility of the Company&#146;s
management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion based on our audits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the
financial statement schedule referred to above, when considered in relation to
the basic financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly in all
material respects the information set forth therein.</font></p>
